paper_metadata.title: Effect of carbon on the tensile properties of Nb-Mo-W alloys at 1773 K

evidence.quote: Ternary Nb±Mo±W alloys of various composition and carbon and oxygen contents were prepared to investigate the deformation and fracture behavior by tensile and compression tests at 1773 K.
Tensile and compressive yield stresses of Nb± X at.% Mo±5 at.% W (hereafter denoted as Nb± XMo±5W, where X is the Mo content) at 1773 K are plotted in Fig. 1 as a function of Mo content.
Most of the samples tested were controlled to be about 200 wt.ppm (hereafter denoted as ppm) for oxygen content.

The base Nb±5Mo±15W alloy is clearly composed of single-phase b.c.c.

carbide precipitates both along grain boundaries and within grains in Nb±5Mo±15W±0.5C
When the carbon content is increased to 1 at.%, carbide is seen to precipitate not only along grain boundaries but also within grains.
On further increasing the carbon content to 4 at.%, the carbide layer becomes larger.
The average grain size of the base Nb±5Mo±15W alloy with equiaxed microstructure was estimated to be about 40 mm.
With increasing carbon content, carbide is found to precipitate along grain boundaries, but not within grains
Carbide along grain boundaries becomes thick with increasing carbon content from 0.1 to 0.5 at.%.
A typical intergranular fracture is observed in Nb±5Mo±15W without carbon addition (Fig. 8a).
Transgranular fracture is seen with striations on the fracture surfaces, indicating that activation of dislocation slip occurs in Nb±5Mo±5W alloy.
intergranular fracture takes place in Nb±35Mo±5W alloy
the fracture mode is changed from intergranular to transgranular fracture with river patterns indicating cleavage fracture (Fig. 8c)
In Nb±5Mo±15W±1C and Nb±5Mo±15W±4C, a quasi-cleavage fracture consisting of fibrous patterns and cleavage fracture surfaces is observed (Fig. 8d,e).
A mixed fracture mode consisting of intergranular and transgranular fracture is observed in the Nb±5Mo±15W±0.1C alloy (Fig. 8b).
In the alloy with low oxygen content, the fracture surface appears to consist of homogeneous fibrous patterns without intergranular facets, which are generated by plastic deformation at 1773 K.
This result can be ascribed to weak grain boundaries due to oxygen segregation.
The compressive yield stress increases with increasing Mo content in Nb± XMo±5W.
the tensile yield stress increases with increasing Mo content up to 15%
This alloy is very brittle and fractures without showing yielding at a very low stress of about 180 MPa.
the alloy containing 2444 ppm O fractures at low stress without plastic yielding
Nb± XMo±5W alloys exhibit marked solid solution strengthening with increasing Mo content in compression tests.
This result can be ascribed to weak grain boundaries due to oxygen segregation.
when the grain interior of an alloy is strengthened by precipitates, the alloy tends to exhibit intergranular fracture
when grain boundary carbide can interrupt boundary sliding by which intergranular fracture initiates, fracture stress will increase
Nb± XMo±5W alloys exhibit marked solid solution strengthening with increasing Mo content in compression tests.
complete intergranular fracture takes place, corresponding to the low fracture stress of this sample. This result can be ascribed to weak grain boundaries due to oxygen segregation.
Intergranular fracture is suppressed by precipitation of Nb2C along grain boundaries and ductility increases on addition of an appropriate amount of carbon.
Transgranular fracture is seen with striations on the fracture surfaces, indicating that activation of dislocation slip occurs in Nb±5Mo±5W alloy.
